claims.text: The Palace of Westminster, widely known as the Houses of Parliament, is the historic meeting place for the Parliament of the United Kingdom.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building is often referred to as the 'Mother of All Parliaments' because of its profound influence on democratic systems around the world.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Originally built in the eleventh century, it served as the primary residence of English kings until a devastating fire destroyed the royal apartments in 1512.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1834, a second massive fire destroyed most of the palace, but the eleventh century Westminster Hall miraculously survived.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The present building was designed in the 19th century by Charles Barry in a splendid Perpendicular Gothic style.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Barry's assistant, the passionate Gothic architect Augustus Pugin, famously complained that the building's symmetrical layout was too classical, grumbling that it was 'Tudor details on a classic body'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The massive complex contains over 1,100 rooms, 100 staircases, and 3 miles of passageways spread over four floors.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The House of Commons, where elected Members of Parliament meet, is located in the northern part of the building and is distinctly decorated with green leather upholstery.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The House of Lords, situated in the southern half of the palace, is decorated with rich red leather upholstery to distinguish it from the Commons.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the Second World War, the palace suffered extensive bomb damage that required the entire House of Commons chamber to be completely rebuilt.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1987, the palace was officially designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site alongside Westminster Abbey and St Margaret's Church.
claims.subject: self
